# Company 077 — Data Redaction / Tokenization API

**Company ID:** `company:future:077`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:077`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-077-v1.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no customer content processing or token vault deployment.

## Business identity
Purpose: remove, mask, pseudonymize or tokenize sensitive information before data is stored, shared, analyzed, logged or sent to AI systems.

## Product tree
Text Redaction API; Structured Field Tokenization; Database Proxy/Transformer; Document/PDF Redaction; Image/Screenshot Redaction; Log Redaction; Support/Conversation Redaction; Prompt/Output Privacy Gateway; Test-Data Pseudonymization; Reversible Token Vault; Irreversible Masking; Format-Preserving Transformation; Policy/Field Rules; Regional Policy Packs; Quality Verification; Batch/Streaming; SDK/CLI; Private/Self-Hosted; Enterprise Gateway.

## Feature/customer/vertical tree
Features: detected data class, field/path/region, transform policy, reversible/irreversible mode, token namespace, format-preserving rules, key/vault reference, output hash, coverage/confidence, missed-sensitive-data tests, false-redaction review, retention and audit.
Customers: SaaS, enterprises, AI platforms, support vendors, analytics teams, developers, privacy/security teams and regulated organizations.
Verticals: health admin, finance-adjacent, HR, support, analytics, software logs, ecommerce and AI/RAG workflows.

## Brain capability / architecture
Brain may identify ambiguous sensitive context; transformation should be deterministic once policy/class is known. Architecture: classifier/detector interface, policy engine, transform library, tokenization vault/HSM adapter, namespace/key management, document/image processors, quality evaluator, audit/provenance and regional routing.

## Agent tree
Policy Mapping Agent; Redaction Agent; Tokenization Agent; Document/Image Agent; QA/Coverage Agent; False-Positive Review Agent; Privacy Gateway Agent; Key/Vault Coordinator; Incident Agent.

## Deterministic services
Mask/hash/token functions; format preservation; vault lookup; key/reference isolation; structured path selectors; OCR/image boxes; reversible mapping ACL; batch/stream idempotency; quality tests; secure deletion of temporary plaintext.

## Workflow
Input authorized → detect/classify sensitive fields → select policy/purpose/region → transform/tokenize → verify expected classes removed/protected → emit sanitized artifact + evidence → downstream use → detokenize only for explicitly authorized purpose/actor → audit access → rotate/delete tokens per policy.

## Integrations / API / data
PII discovery, databases, ETL, logs, support, AI gateways, warehouses, test environments, document/image pipelines, vault/KMS. Data: policy metadata, token mappings where reversible, hashes, quality findings and audit; raw plaintext minimized.

## Monetization / distribution
Records/characters/GB, token-vault entries, API calls, connectors, enterprise/private, policy packs and managed privacy gateway. Distribution via privacy/security/data/AI ecosystems.

## Security/privacy/compliance
Token vault is critical infrastructure: strong encryption, split access, key rotation, regional isolation, no logs with plaintext, least privilege and purpose-bound detokenization. Redaction is not proof of anonymization unless evaluated for the use case.

## Failure / edge cases
Missed entity, over-redaction, nested JSON, free text, OCR error, structured IDs embedded in images, token collision, format-preserving weakness, key loss, wrong namespace, reversible token exposed, downstream join requirements, deletion request, regional migration.

## Scale / overlap
API → privacy gateway → data transformation infrastructure. Overlap #76 discovery, #78 retention, #98 sovereignty. #077 owns transformation/protection.

## Classification
**DESIGN NOW:** sensitivity labels, transform policy metadata, secret/key refs, purpose-bound access, reversible/irreversible distinction and provenance.  
**BUILD NOW:** Command Center should have standard redaction/tokenization seams before historical/external data enters Brain/Agency/logs.  
**BUILD BEFORE FIRST COMPANY:** token vault, data transformers and customer gateway.  
**COMPANY-SPECIFIC LATER:** connectors/policy packs/customer billing.  
**SCALE-ONLY:** globally distributed regional token vaults.

# Mandatory 24-part completion block
1. Product Tree: text/structured/DB/docs/images/logs/support/AI/test data/token vault/masking/format preserving/policy/QA/batch/private.
2. Feature Tree: class/path/region/policy/mode/namespace/key ref/hash/coverage/confidence/retention/audit.
3. Customer Tree: SaaS/enterprise/AI/support/analytics/dev/privacy/security/regulated.
4. Vertical Tree: health admin/finance/HR/support/analytics/logs/commerce/AI.
5. Brain Tree: ambiguous detection only; transformation deterministic.
6. Agent Tree: policy/redact/tokenize/doc-image/QA/review/gateway/vault/incident.
7. Service Tree: mask/hash/token/format/vault/key refs/selectors/OCR/idempotency/quality/secure deletion.
8. Workflow Tree: classify→policy→transform→verify→sanitized output→authorized detokenize→audit/rotate/delete.
9. Integration Tree: discovery/DB/ETL/logs/support/AI/warehouse/tests/docs/vault.
10. Data Tree: policies/tokens/hashes/quality/audit with minimal plaintext.
11. API Tree: redact/tokenize/detokenize/verify/policy/audit.
12. Monetization Tree: records/chars/GB/tokens/calls/connectors/enterprise/packs.
13. Distribution Tree: privacy/security/data/AI/OEM.
14. Automation Tree: transform/verify automatic; detokenization tightly authorized.
15. Moat Tree: accuracy, format coverage, policy packs, vault reliability.
16. Platform Tree: redaction API→privacy gateway→data protection infrastructure.
17. Risk Tree: missed PII/over-redaction/token leak/key loss/weak pseudonymization/region violation.
18. Scale Tree: API→enterprise gateway→regional global vaults.
19. Spinoff Tree: token vault/image redaction modules; discovery/retention remain separate.
20. Command Center Dependencies: sensitivity, secrets/KMS refs, privacy, artifacts, provider routing, audit.
21. Design-Now Requirements: standardized redaction/pseudonymization metadata and purpose-bound access.
22. Build-Now Requirements: ensure Command Center ingest/log/context paths can apply deterministic redaction before AI exposure.
23. Safe-to-Defer Requirements: commercial vault/connectors/global regions.
24. Autonomous Mature State: sensitive data is transformed at ingress by policy; humans manage exceptional classifications and privileged detokenization.

## Saturation result
Further branches converge into discovery, retention, sovereignty or privacy-request products already represented.

# Company 078 — Data Retention & Deletion Autopilot

**Company ID:** `company:future:078`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:078`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-078-v1.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no customer deletion, retention change, legal-hold release or production data mutation.

## Business identity
Purpose: enforce defined data lifecycles across databases, files, logs, analytics, backups, embeddings, agent memory and third-party systems with legal holds, exceptions and deletion evidence.

## Product tree
Retention Policy Registry; Data Inventory Link; Lifecycle Classifier; Expiry Scheduler; Deletion Orchestrator; Archive/Tiering; Legal Hold; Customer/Account Deletion Workflow; Backup Retention Tracker; Log/Telemetry Retention; Vector/Embedding Deletion; Agent/AI Memory Deletion; Vendor/Subprocessor Deletion; Restore-Window Manager; Exception/Approval Queue; Deletion Verification/Reconciliation; Evidence Certificate; Policy Simulator; API/SDK; Enterprise/Private Deployment; Jurisdiction/Industry Packs.

## Feature/customer/vertical tree
Features: data object/class, owner, subject/account/project/company, source system, purpose, creation/last-use, policy/version, retention period, expiry, hold, exception, backup copy, derived copy, vendor copy, deletion task/result, verification, restore window and evidence.
Customers: enterprises, SaaS, privacy/security/data governance, AI platforms, MSPs and regulated organizations.
Verticals: consumer apps, HR, health admin, finance-adjacent, support, analytics, ecommerce, data/AI systems and enterprise records.

## Brain capability / architecture
Brain may map ambiguous data to retention policy and explain exceptions. Deterministic policy/version and inventory lineage own expiry/deletion eligibility. No AI may release legal holds or delete uncertain data autonomously.

Architecture: data inventory/lineage, policy/version registry, lifecycle scheduler, legal-hold registry, system connector registry, deletion DAG, tombstone/verification records, backup/derived-data tracking, vendor tasks, reconciliation, audit and protected deletion gate.

## Agent tree
Policy Mapping Agent; Data Lifecycle Agent; Expiry Agent; Legal Hold Agent; Deletion Coordinator; Backup Agent; Derived-Data Agent; Vendor Deletion Agent; Reconciliation Agent; Evidence Agent; Privacy/Compliance QA Agent.

## Deterministic services
Retention arithmetic; policy precedence; hold checks; immutable tombstones; deletion idempotency; dependency/lineage traversal; backup expiration tracking; retries/DLQ; deletion receipts; restoration-window rules; evidence hashing.

## Workflow
Inventory/classify data → bind exact policy/version → compute expiry → hold/exception evaluation → schedule → protected deletion/archival plan → execute per-system tasks → collect receipts → follow derived/vendor/backup copies → reconcile unresolved remnants → certify outcome or explicit exception → retain minimal evidence.

## Integrations / API / data
Databases, object/file storage, logs, warehouses, SaaS, backups, vector stores, model/agent memory, analytics, vendors/subprocessors, data catalogs and privacy systems. Data: policies, inventory refs, lifecycle states, holds, tasks, receipts, exceptions and evidence.

## Monetization / distribution
Data sources/objects/GB, deletion tasks, policies, connectors, seats, enterprise/private, managed governance and jurisdiction packs. Distribution via privacy/data-governance/security ecosystems.

## Security/privacy/compliance
Deletion is destructive and legally sensitive. Strong authority, legal holds, immutable evidence, no over-deletion, privacy-preserving proof, backup limitations, vendor reconciliation, regional rules and restore/safe windows where appropriate.

## Failure / edge cases
Legal hold added during deletion, eventual-consistency replicas, backup restore reintroduces deleted data, derived embeddings/models, shared records for multiple subjects, partial vendor deletion, system offline, retention conflict, audit records themselves requiring retention, account merge/split. Explicit exception states are mandatory.

## Scale / overlap
Single policy → enterprise lifecycle → global retention/deletion control plane. Overlap #47 DSAR, #76 discovery, #77 redaction, #94 lineage. #078 owns lifecycle enforcement.

## Classification
**DESIGN NOW:** retention/expiry/hold/exception metadata, deletion tombstones, lineage/dependency refs, protected destructive action, backup/derived-data awareness.  
**BUILD NOW:** Command Center memory/artifact/log/history systems need explicit retention/deletion semantics now to avoid retrofit.  
**BUILD BEFORE FIRST COMPANY:** external connector/deletion orchestration and customer policy registry.  
**COMPANY-SPECIFIC LATER:** jurisdiction packs/customer UI/pricing.  
**SCALE-ONLY:** global distributed deletion and massive backup/vendor reconciliation.

# Company 079 — Digital Provenance / Authenticity Platform

**Company ID:** `company:future:079`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:079`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-079-v1.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no public certificate issuance, legal attestation or external publication.

## Business identity
Purpose: record and verify who/what created, modified, approved and transformed digital artifacts across documents, media, code, datasets and AI/agent outputs.

## Product tree
Artifact Identity Registry; Hash/Timestamp Service; Creator/Agent/Model Identity Binding; Edit/Transformation History; Approval/Attestation Chain; Chain-of-Custody; Signature/Certificate Service; Tamper Detection; AI-Generation Provenance; Dataset/Model Provenance; Code/Build Provenance; Contract/Record Provenance; Media Authenticity; Public Verification Page/API; Embedded Verification SDK; Evidence Export; Legal-Hold Integration; Enterprise Private Ledger; Cross-Organization Trust Adapter.

## Feature/customer/vertical tree
Features: artifact ID/version/hash, parent/derived refs, creator/owner, agent/model/runtime/version, source inputs, transformation tool/version, timestamp, signature, approval, policy, location/environment, evidence, revocation/supersession and verification result.
Customers: enterprises, media, AI vendors, software teams, legal/compliance, data companies, marketplaces, creators and government/public-sector record systems.
Verticals: media/news, enterprise documents, AI output, software supply chain, research/data, contracts, regulated records and digital assets.

## Brain capability / architecture
Brain may explain lineage and flag suspicious inconsistencies; authenticity must be established through cryptographic hashes/signatures, trusted identity and provenance records—not model opinion. Architecture: immutable append-only provenance graph, artifact store references, signing/KMS adapter, timestamping, identity/trust registry, verification engine, revocation/supersession, public/private proof views.

## Agent tree
Provenance Collector; Artifact Identity Agent; Signature Coordinator; Lineage Agent; Tamper Analyst; AI Provenance Agent; Chain-of-Custody Agent; Verification Agent; Evidence Export Agent; Incident/Revocation Agent.

## Deterministic services
Content hashing; Merkle/graph links; signatures; timestamp verification; certificate validation; lineage traversal; version/supersession; immutable append; proof packaging; privacy-aware disclosure.

## Workflow
Artifact created/imported → compute identity/hash → bind creator/runtime/model/source → append transformation/approval events → sign/timestamp as policy requires → downstream transformation references parent → verification recomputes hashes/signatures/chain → return proof/status → revoke/supersede compromised claims without erasing history.

## Integrations / API / data
Document/media systems, source control/build systems, AI gateways, data catalogs, asset stores, KMS/signing, identity/trust systems, marketplaces and compliance archives. Data: provenance metadata, hashes, signatures, identities and lineage; raw artifact may remain in source storage.

## Monetization / distribution
Artifacts/proofs/verifications/signatures, storage/retention, enterprise/private, API/SDK, public verification, compliance packs. Distribution via AI/media/software/data/legal ecosystems.

## Security/privacy/compliance
Do not expose private lineage publicly by default; proof disclosures scoped, signing keys protected, revocation supported, timestamps/identities trustworthy, no claim that provenance proves truth of artifact content—only origin/chain assertions.

## Failure / edge cases
Hash canonicalization, mutable formats/metadata, key compromise, copied artifact without provenance, offline creation, missing ancestor, clock issues, identity compromise, model alias drift, partial chain across companies, redacted source, proprietary input that cannot be disclosed.

## Scale / overlap
Artifact signing → enterprise provenance graph → cross-organization authenticity infrastructure. Overlap #5 AI audit, #94 data lineage, #91 agent identity. #079 owns artifact authenticity/chain-of-custody.

## Classification
**DESIGN NOW:** stable artifact IDs/hashes, immutable lineage, creator/agent/model/runtime refs, supersession/revocation and evidence disclosure boundaries.  
**BUILD NOW:** Command Center already depends on artifact hashes/evidence; reverse-map says provenance should be unified rather than per-module.  
**BUILD BEFORE FIRST COMPANY:** signing/trust/public proof layers.  
**COMPANY-SPECIFIC LATER:** public verification/commercial certificate products.  
**SCALE-ONLY:** federated global provenance network.

# Mandatory 24-part completion block
1. Product Tree: registry/hash/timestamp/identity/edit/approval/custody/sign/tamper/AI/data/code/contracts/media/public verify/SDK/evidence/private ledger.
2. Feature Tree: artifact/version/hash/parents/creator/agent/model/source/tool/time/signature/approval/policy/env/revocation/status.

4. Vertical Tree: media/docs/AI/software/research/contracts/regulated records/digital assets.
5. Brain Tree: lineage explanation/anomaly flagging; proof cryptographic/deterministic.
6. Agent Tree: collector/identity/signature/lineage/tamper/AI provenance/custody/verify/export/revoke.
7. Service Tree: hashing/graph/signatures/timestamps/cert validation/lineage/version/append/proof/disclosure.
8. Workflow Tree: create→hash/bind→append→sign→derive→verify→prove→revoke/supersede.

11. API Tree: register/append/sign/verify/lineage/proof/revoke.
12. Monetization Tree: artifacts/proofs/verifications/signatures/retention/enterprise/API.
13. Distribution Tree: AI/media/software/data/legal/OEM.
14. Automation Tree: capture/hash/verify automatic; legal/public attestations governed.
15. Moat Tree: provenance graph, interoperability, trust integrations, verification ubiquity.
16. Platform Tree: provenance service→authenticity network→digital trust infrastructure.
17. Risk Tree: key/identity compromise/privacy leakage/false trust/missing lineage/canonicalization errors.
18. Scale Tree: artifact→enterprise graph→federated network.
19. Spinoff Tree: public verification/signing modules; agent identity/data lineage remain adjacent.
20. Command Center Dependencies: artifact registry, evidence, identity, Brain/Agency model refs, KMS, audit.
21. Design-Now Requirements: one canonical provenance envelope for artifacts, AI outputs, decisions and builds.
22. Build-Now Requirements: unify Command Center artifact/evidence lineage and immutable hashes before further factories depend on them.
23. Safe-to-Defer Requirements: public trust network/signature commercial service.
24. Autonomous Mature State: provenance capture/verification is invisible and automatic; humans manage trust roots, key incidents and public/legal attestations.
